correctness.rationale: Finite discrete variation makes the sequence a uniformly convergent superposition of translated unit steps plus its left limit. The derivative of the reconstruction is the same translated sum in L¹ because the unit-step derivative is compactly supported; hence its L¹ norm is exactly the sharp induced norm, attained by a single step. Each side cell has one hump of magnitude 4|λ|/27 and equal endpoint values, giving 16|λ|/27 in total. With z=2t−1, the central derivative is (3−λ)/2+3(λ−1)z²/2 and its signed integral is one. For λ<0 its positive arc has integral (3−λ)q/3, where q²=(3−λ)/(3(1−λ)), giving J=2(3−λ)q/3−1. For λ>3 the negative central arc has absolute integral (λ−3)q/3, giving J=1+2(λ−3)q/3. In between the derivative is nonnegative; λ=0 has endpoint zeros and λ=3 a double midpoint zero. This checks the fractional-power excess and both endpoints. Since J≥1 and the side contribution vanishes only at λ=0, that is the only nonexpansive member. The Hermite slopes reproduce nonconstant affine data exactly only at λ=1/2, where the norm is 35/27.
residual_risks: No finite-grid boundary closure is analyzed. The smoothness excess at λ=3 has exponent 3/2, not a breakpoint at 3/2. The uploaded finite test was not replayed and is not needed for the analytic result.

value.rationale: The exact variation cost is a natural stability criterion for the classical cardinal four-tap family. The parameter law quantifies all signs and the change beyond the central double-zero threshold. It also resolves a structural tradeoff: the only nonexpansive parameter loses affine reproduction, whereas the uniquely affine-reproducing one has a strict cost. The claim is useful as an interpolation stability benchmark, not as a new interpolation method or a re-report of the standard-parameter value.
